checks.label: BLE privacy keywords (heuristic)
checks.description: BLE privacy features reduce tracking.
checks.remediation: Enable BLE privacy in developer options or verify via: dumpsys bluetooth_manager | grep -i privacy.
checks.why: BLE privacy features reduce tracking.
checks.risk_if_fail: If absent, privacy may still be enabled but not shown; treat as unknown.

checks.label: Adapter address exposure via settings (should be restricted)
checks.description: Restricting access to the adapter address reduces app-level fingerprinting.
checks.remediation: Clear the stored address: settings delete secure bluetooth_address. Restrict app access to BT address via permissions.
checks.why: Restricting access to the adapter address reduces app-level fingerprinting.
checks.risk_if_fail: If a stable address is exposed, it can be used to correlate the device across contexts.

checks.label: cmd bluetooth_manager dump (inventory)
checks.description: cmd bluetooth_manager may expose structured state useful for auditing.
checks.remediation: Review output manually. If unexpected state is found, disable Bluetooth: settings put global bluetooth_on 0.
checks.why: cmd bluetooth_manager may expose structured state useful for auditing.
checks.risk_if_fail: If unavailable, rely on settings/dumpsys checks.

checks.label: BLE scan always available
checks.description: Always-available BLE scanning can undermine user expectations and privacy.
checks.remediation: Disable always-on BLE scanning: settings put global ble_scan_always_enabled 0.
checks.why: Always-available BLE scanning can undermine user expectations and privacy.
checks.risk_if_fail: If enabled, passive BLE collection/tracking can occur even when the user thinks BT is off.

checks.label: Bluetooth toggle state
checks.description: Minimize radio exposure by keeping Bluetooth disabled when not needed.
checks.remediation: Disable Bluetooth when not in use: settings put global bluetooth_on 0.
checks.why: Minimize radio exposure by keeping Bluetooth disabled when not needed.
checks.risk_if_fail: If Bluetooth is ON continuously, the device is always reachable over a proximity channel.

checks.label: Global Bluetooth-related settings inventory
checks.description: Inventorying settings keys helps detect OEM knobs that override UI expectations.
checks.remediation: Review each listed key manually. Remove or reset unexpected keys via: settings delete global <key_name>.
checks.why: Inventorying settings keys helps detect OEM knobs that override UI expectations.
checks.risk_if_fail: Hidden keys may keep BT discoverable, scanning, or logging enabled.

checks.label: Secure Bluetooth-related settings inventory
checks.description: Secure settings commonly store HCI snoop and adapter identity keys.
checks.remediation: Review each listed key manually. Disable HCI snoop if found: settings put secure bluetooth_hci_log 0.
checks.why: Secure settings commonly store HCI snoop and adapter identity keys.
checks.risk_if_fail: Mis-set secure keys can enable sensitive logging.

checks.label: Third-party Bluetooth packages (non-system)
checks.description: Third-party BT apps can increase attack surface.
checks.remediation: Uninstall suspicious third-party BT apps: pm uninstall <package_name>.
checks.why: Third-party BT apps can increase attack surface.
checks.risk_if_fail: Overprivileged or malicious BT-related apps can abuse the BT subsystem.

checks.label: Disabled Bluetooth packages present
checks.description: Unexpectedly disabled BT packages can indicate tampering or broken policy.
checks.remediation: Re-enable or uninstall disabled BT packages: pm enable <package_name> or pm uninstall <package_name>.
checks.why: Unexpectedly disabled BT packages can indicate tampering or broken policy.
checks.risk_if_fail: If core components are disabled, device may behave unpredictably or rely on vendor replacements.

checks.label: List Bluetooth-related packages
checks.description: Inventory of BT packages helps detect overlays/replacements.
checks.remediation: Review listed packages. Remove unexpected BT packages: pm uninstall <package_name>.
checks.why: Inventory of BT packages helps detect overlays/replacements.
checks.risk_if_fail: Unexpected packages may add attack surface or intercept BT operations.

checks.label: Path of core BT package (com.android.bluetooth)
checks.description: Validating the install path helps ensure the BT stack is system-managed.
checks.remediation: Verify path starts with /system/. If non-system, investigate tampering and restore from factory image.
checks.why: Validating the install path helps ensure the BT stack is system-managed.
checks.risk_if_fail: If path is absent or non-system, it may indicate replacement/tampering.
checks.expected_secure_state: Must resolve to a system path

checks.label: Bluetooth library name
checks.description: Library identifier helps correlate OEM components.
checks.remediation: Record the library name for inventory. Cross-reference with known OEM components for supply-chain review.
checks.why: Library identifier helps correlate OEM components.
checks.risk_if_fail: Unexpected values may require supply-chain review.

checks.label: Android version (inventory)
checks.description: OS version influences which Bluetooth security features exist.
checks.remediation: Update to the latest Android version via system settings to get modern BT hardening features.
checks.why: OS version influences which Bluetooth security features exist.
checks.risk_if_fail: Older OS versions may lack modern Bluetooth hardening.

checks.label: Bluetooth-related properties snapshot
checks.description: Property inventory can reveal debug/logging/test toggles.
checks.remediation: Review properties for debug/test toggles. Remove unsafe ones: setprop <property_name> "" (requires root).
checks.why: Property inventory can reveal debug/logging/test toggles.
checks.risk_if_fail: Mis-set properties can silently reduce security.

checks.label: Adapter scan mode
checks.description: Extracts the adapter scan mode constants from the Bluetooth manager dump. The earlier version grepped case-insensitively for the phrase 'scan mode', which on a Samsung device matches the line 'Scan mode counter (Opp/LowPower/Balanced/LowLatency/AmbientDiscovery)', a statistics counter rather than the adapter mode. That text never contains SCAN_MODE_CONNECTABLE, so the check reported a critical finding on every such device. The pattern is anchored: SCAN_MODE_CONNECTABLE_DISCOVERABLE contains SCAN_MODE_CONNECTABLE as a prefix, so an unanchored pattern passed a discoverable adapter, which is the exact condition the check exists to catch.
checks.remediation: Set scan mode to non-discoverable. Avoid CONNECTABLE_DISCOVERABLE outside active pairing windows.
checks.why: Discoverability should be OFF by default and used only briefly for pairing.
checks.risk_if_fail: If CONNECTABLE_DISCOVERABLE, attackers can easily find and target the device.

checks.label: Discoverable timeout (if reported)
checks.description: Timeout limits exposure window while discoverable.
checks.remediation: Set a short discoverable timeout (120s or less) in Bluetooth settings or via OEM configuration.
checks.why: Timeout limits exposure window while discoverable.
checks.risk_if_fail: Long/indefinite discoverability increases enumeration and tracking risk.
checks.notes: Field varies by Android/OEM; if absent, rely on BT-010.

checks.label: Discoverability settings keys (OEM-dependent inventory)
checks.description: Some OEMs expose discoverability toggles via global settings keys.
checks.remediation: Review listed keys. Set discoverability to off: settings put global <discover_key> 0.
checks.why: Some OEMs expose discoverability toggles via global settings keys.
checks.risk_if_fail: If present and set incorrectly, device may remain discoverable.

checks.label: Encryption key length (KNOB risk heuristic)
checks.description: Key length negotiation should not be downgraded.
checks.remediation: Ensure patch level addresses CVE-2019-9506 (KNOB). Update device firmware to enforce 128-bit key length.
checks.why: Key length negotiation should not be downgraded.
checks.risk_if_fail: Weak key lengths can enable brute-force decryption (e.g., KNOB-style entropy reduction on vulnerable stacks).
checks.notes: If key length isn't printed, validate via patch level and SC enforcement.
checks.expected_secure_state: Key length should indicate 16 octets / 128-bit when reported

checks.label: Profile keywords present: HFP/HSP (Handsfree)
checks.description: Disabling unused profiles reduces attack surface.
checks.remediation: Disable HFP/HSP if not needed. Remove profile via Bluetooth app settings or disable in developer options.
checks.why: Disabling unused profiles reduces attack surface.
checks.risk_if_fail: Extra profiles can expose sensitive data/services to paired devices.
checks.notes: If output is non-empty, confirm whether profile is enabled/connected and whether it is required.
checks.expected_secure_state: Unused profiles should be disabled; if present, must be justified

checks.label: dumpsys snoop indicators
checks.description: Some builds include runtime snoop mode info in dumpsys.
checks.remediation: Disable snoop logging: settings put secure bluetooth_hci_log 0. Delete existing snoop files.
checks.why: Some builds include runtime snoop mode info in dumpsys.
checks.risk_if_fail: If enabled, debugging capture may expose sensitive artifacts.

checks.label: Snoop-related properties snapshot
checks.description: OEMs sometimes control logging via properties.
checks.remediation: Remove snoop-related properties: setprop persist.bluetooth.btsnoopenable false (requires root).
checks.why: OEMs sometimes control logging via properties.
checks.risk_if_fail: Forced-on logging can persist across reboots.

checks.label: Secure setting bluetooth_hci_log
checks.description: HCI snoop logging is a debug feature and should be disabled outside troubleshooting.
checks.remediation: Disable HCI snoop logging: settings put secure bluetooth_hci_log 0.
checks.why: HCI snoop logging is a debug feature and should be disabled outside troubleshooting.
checks.risk_if_fail: If enabled, sensitive Bluetooth traffic/metadata may be written and later exfiltrated.

checks.label: Just Works usage indicators
checks.description: Just Works provides no MITM protection.
checks.remediation: Avoid Just Works pairing. Use Numeric Comparison or Passkey Entry for MITM-resistant association.
checks.why: Just Works provides no MITM protection.
checks.risk_if_fail: If used, an active attacker can MITM the pairing/association.

checks.label: Secure Connections (SC) indicators
checks.description: Secure Connections strengthens pairing/key agreement.
checks.remediation: Enable Secure Connections on the device. Update firmware if SC is not supported by the current stack.
checks.why: Secure Connections strengthens pairing/key agreement.
checks.risk_if_fail: If SC is absent/disabled, device may accept legacy association and weaker keying.

checks.label: SELinux Bluetooth Domain Policy
checks.command: C=$( (ps -A -Z 2>/dev/null || /system/bin/ps -A -Z) | grep -m1 -iE 'com\.android\.bluetooth|bluetooth' | awk '{print $1}'); [ -z "$C" ] && echo BLUETOOTH_NOT_RUNNING || echo "$C"
checks.description: Reports the SELinux context of the running Bluetooth process. The earlier version ran 'ls -Z /system/bin/bluetooth*', a path that has not existed since Bluetooth became an APK rather than a native daemon, so the ls failed on every modern device and the check reported PERMISSIVE universally. Now reads the context of the live process, and reports BLUETOOTH_NOT_RUNNING when the stack is not up rather than failing.
checks.remediation: Verify BT binary SELinux label: ls -Z /system/bin/bluetooth*. Re-label or restore from factory if wrong.

checks.label: Bluetooth Daemon Hardening
checks.command: P=$( (ps -A -o cmd 2>/dev/null || /system/bin/ps -A -o cmd 2>/dev/null) ); if [ -z "$P" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no process listing available"; elif printf '%s\n' "$P" | grep -E 'bluetoothd|bluetooth' | grep -q -- '-n'; then echo HARDENED; else echo CHECK_REQUIRED; fi
checks.description: The Bluetooth daemon should run with the '-n' flag (no‑privilege mode) to prevent loading unnecessary plugins.
checks.remediation: Configure bluetoothd to run with -n flag. Edit init scripts or verify daemon configuration.

checks.label: Airplane Mode Enforces BT Off
checks.command: APM=$(settings get global airplane_mode_on 2>/dev/null); BT=$(settings get global bluetooth_on 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$APM$BT" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED settings get returned nothing"; else echo "AirplaneMode=${APM:-unset} BT=${BT:-unset}"; fi
checks.description: When airplane mode is on, Bluetooth must also be off to prevent RF emissions in restricted environments.
checks.remediation: Ensure airplane mode disables BT: settings put global bluetooth_on 0 when airplane_mode_on is 1.

checks.label: BLE MAC Randomization Status
checks.command: V=$(settings get global bluetooth_address_rotation_enabled 2>/dev/null); case "$V" in 1) echo Enabled;; 0) echo Disabled;; null) echo NotSupported;; "") echo "UNMEASURED settings get returned nothing";; *) echo "UNMEASURED unexpected value";; esac
checks.description: BLE MAC randomization must be enabled to prevent persistent device tracking.
checks.remediation: Enable BLE MAC randomization: settings put global bluetooth_address_rotation_enabled 1.

checks.label: Bluetooth Stack (Not Bluedroid)
checks.command: [ $(getprop ro.bluetooth.stack 2>/dev/null | grep -i bluedroid | wc -l) -gt 0 ] && echo VULNERABLE || echo SAFE
checks.description: The Bluetooth stack should not be Bluedroid (vulnerable to BlueBorne). Fluoride is the modern, hardened replacement.
checks.remediation: Upgrade to a ROM or firmware using the Fluoride stack instead of Bluedroid.

checks.label: Active Connection Encryption
checks.command: D=$(dumpsys bluetooth_manager 2>/dev/null); case "$D" in ""|*"Can't find service"*|*"Failure calling service"*|*"Failed transaction"*|*"Found 0 services"*) echo "UNMEASURED dumpsys bluetooth_manager did not answer";; *) A=$(printf '%s\n' "$D" | grep -A 5 'Active Devices:' | grep 'Encrypted' | awk '{print $2}'); if [ -z "$A" ]; then echo "NO_ACTIVE_CONNECTIONS"; elif printf '%s\n' "$A" | grep -q 'false'; then echo FAIL; else echo PASS; fi;; esac
checks.description: All active Bluetooth connections must be encrypted (NIST SC-13).
checks.remediation: Ensure all active connections are encrypted. Unpair and re-pair any device showing unencrypted links.

checks.label: Secure Simple Pairing (SSP) Enabled
checks.command: D=$(dumpsys bluetooth_manager 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$D" ]; then echo UNMEASURED; elif printf '%s\n' "$D" | grep -qi 'Secure Simple Pairing.*Enabled'; then echo Enabled; else echo Disabled; fi
checks.description: SSP must be enabled; otherwise legacy pairing is vulnerable to PIN brute‑force and KNOB downgrade attacks.
checks.remediation: Enable SSP via firmware update or ROM upgrade. Verify: dumpsys bluetooth_manager | grep -i 'Secure Simple Pairing'.

checks.label: Paired Devices Count
checks.command: D=$(dumpsys bluetooth_manager 2>/dev/null); case "$D" in ""|*"Can't find service"*|*"Failure calling service"*|*"Failed transaction"*|*"does not exist"*|*"Found 0 services"*) echo "UNMEASURED dumpsys bluetooth_manager did not answer";; *) printf '%s\n' "$D" | grep 'Bonded devices:' -A 10 | grep 'Device:' | wc -l;; esac
checks.description: Review all paired devices (AC-3)
checks.remediation: Remove all unnecessary paired devices via Settings > Bluetooth > Forget device.

checks.label: Bluetooth Encryption
checks.description: Bluetooth encryption must be enabled (SC-13)
checks.remediation: Ensure encryption is enabled for all BT connections. Re-pair devices if encryption is reported as disabled.

checks.label: Secure Pairing Mode
checks.description: Only secure pairing modes should be allowed (NIST IA-2)
checks.remediation: Set pairing mode to Secure only. Avoid legacy PIN pairing via firmware/ROM configuration.

checks.label: Unnecessary Profiles
checks.description: Disable unused profiles (CM-7)
checks.remediation: Disable unnecessary profiles via Settings > Connected devices or pm disable relevant BT service components.

checks.label: Bonded/Paired Device Audit
checks.description: Manually review bonded devices. Any unknown MAC indicates unauthorized pairing or a silent backdoor.
checks.remediation: Review all bonded MACs. Remove any unknown device via Settings > Bluetooth > Forget device.

checks.label: Legacy Bluetooth Profiles
checks.description: Legacy profiles can expose device to known CVEs - disable if not needed.
checks.remediation: Disable legacy profiles (OBEX, PAN, SAP) via BT settings or: setprop bluetooth.opp false (requires root).

checks.label: Authentication Required
checks.description: Authentication must be required for pairing to prevent BIAS attacks (CVE-2020-10135).
checks.remediation: Ensure authentication is required. Update firmware to enforce mandatory authentication on pairing.

checks.label: Bluetooth Debugging Interface
checks.description: Bluetooth debugging interfaces must be disabled in production (CM-6)
checks.remediation: Disable BT debugging: setprop persist.bluetooth.debug false. Verify no debug flags remain.

checks.label: Link Key Strength (128-bit)
checks.description: Link encryption keys must be at least 128 bits; shorter keys are vulnerable to the KNOB attack.
checks.remediation: Ensure 128-bit link keys. Apply security patches addressing CVE-2019-9506 (KNOB attack).

checks.label: LE Security Mode
checks.description: LE Security Mode must be 2, 3, or 4; Mode 1 or absence enables the BLESA attack (CVE-2020-9770).
checks.remediation: Set LE Security Mode to 2 or higher. Update firmware if only Mode 1 is available.

checks.label: Exposed Profile: HID (Input Device)
checks.command: D=$(dumpsys bluetooth_manager 2>/dev/null); case "$D" in ""|*"Can't find service"*|*"Failure calling service"*|*"Failed transaction"*) echo "UNMEASURED dumpsys bluetooth_manager did not answer; see the HID role property checks";; *) printf '%s\n' "$D" | grep -i -E 'hid|HidService|InputDevice';; esac
checks.description: HID should not be connected; otherwise keystroke injection and BlueBorne RCE (CVE-2017-0785) are possible.
checks.remediation: Disable HID profile when no BT input devices are in use. Disconnect active HID sessions immediately.

checks.label: I/O Capability (Not NoInputNoOutput)
checks.description: I/O capability should allow MITM protection (e.g., DisplayYesNo). NoInputNoOutput forces JustWorks and is insecure.
checks.remediation: Set I/O capability to DisplayYesNo. Avoid NoInputNoOutput to prevent Just Works fallback.

checks.label: Exposed Profile: MAP (Message Access)
checks.description: MAP should be disconnected (mState: 0); otherwise SMS and 2FA codes are remotely readable.
checks.remediation: Disable MAP profile: revoke message access for BT devices in Settings > Connected devices.

checks.label: Exposed Profile: OPP (File Transfer)
checks.description: OPP should be disconnected or not present; otherwise unsolicited file pushes (CVE-2018-9426) are possible.
checks.remediation: Disable OPP profile. Block object push via BT settings or: setprop bluetooth.opp false.

checks.label: Exposed Profile: PBAP (Phonebook)
checks.description: PBAP should be disconnected; otherwise the full contacts database can be exfiltrated silently.
checks.remediation: Disable PBAP: revoke phonebook access for BT devices in Settings > Connected devices.

checks.label: Exposed Profile: SAP (SIM Access)
checks.description: SAP should be disconnected; otherwise a remote device can fully control the SIM card.
checks.remediation: Disable SAP profile immediately: setprop bluetooth.sap false. Remove SIM access for all BT devices.

checks.label: BLE UUID/Service Advertisement
checks.description: No active BLE advertisements should be present; they leak device fingerprints even with MAC randomization.
checks.remediation: Stop BLE advertisements when not needed. Review and disable advertising apps via BT developer options.

checks.label: Encryption on Active Connections
checks.description: All active Bluetooth connections must be encrypted; otherwise raw HCI payload can be captured by passive radio sniffing.
checks.remediation: Ensure all connections are encrypted. Disconnect and re-pair any device with unencrypted links.

checks.label: Exposed Profile: PAN (Network Access)
checks.description: PAN tethering (mTetherOn) must be false to prevent unauthorized network access and traffic interception.
checks.remediation: Disable PAN tethering: Settings > Network > Tethering > Bluetooth tethering off.

checks.label: Bluetooth Stack Version
checks.description: Check the Bluetooth stack version against the latest for your Android version; outdated versions may contain known CVEs.
checks.remediation: Update the Bluetooth stack to the latest version via system update or security patch.

checks.label: Apps with BLUETOOTH_CONNECT Permission
checks.command: D=$(dumpsys package 2>/dev/null); case "$D" in ""|*"Can't find service"*|*"Failure calling service"*|*"Failed transaction"*|*"does not exist"*|*"Found 0 services"*) echo "UNMEASURED dumpsys package did not answer";; *) printf '%s\n' "$D" | grep -B5 'BLUETOOTH_CONNECT' | grep 'packageName' | sort -u | wc -l;; esac
checks.description: Fewer than six apps should hold BLUETOOTH_CONNECT; over‑permissioned apps can expose MACs and connection states.
checks.remediation: Revoke BLUETOOTH_CONNECT from unnecessary apps: pm revoke <package> android.permission.BLUETOOTH_CONNECT.

checks.label: bluetooth.opp Property
checks.command: S=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); V=$(getprop persist.bluetooth.profile.opp.enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] && V=$(getprop bluetooth.profile.opp.enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] && V=$(getprop bluetooth.opp 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$V" ] && [ -z "$S" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED getprop unavailable"; elif [ -z "$V" ]; then echo "opp=not_set"; else echo "opp=$V"; fi
checks.description: Object Push Profile accepts inbound file transfers. Historically the richest Bluetooth attack surface on Android and unnecessary on a fixed install.
checks.remediation: Disable the profile in the product build: set persist.bluetooth.profile.opp.enabled=false, or remove it from the enabled profile list in the Bluetooth APEX config, then reboot.

checks.label: bluetooth.pan Property
checks.command: S=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); V=$(getprop persist.bluetooth.profile.pan.nap.enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] && V=$(getprop bluetooth.profile.pan.nap.enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] && V=$(getprop bluetooth.pan 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$V" ] && [ -z "$S" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED getprop unavailable"; elif [ -z "$V" ]; then echo "pan=not_set"; else echo "pan=$V"; fi
checks.description: PAN Network Access Point makes the device act as a network router for bonded peers, bridging Bluetooth range into the wired or wireless network behind it.
checks.remediation: Disable the profile in the product build: set persist.bluetooth.profile.pan.nap.enabled=false, or remove it from the enabled profile list in the Bluetooth APEX config, then reboot.

checks.label: bluetooth.pbap Property
checks.command: S=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); V=$(getprop persist.bluetooth.profile.pbap.server.enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] && V=$(getprop bluetooth.profile.pbap.server.enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] && V=$(getprop bluetooth.pbap 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$V" ] && [ -z "$S" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED getprop unavailable"; elif [ -z "$V" ]; then echo "pbap=not_set"; else echo "pbap=$V"; fi
checks.description: Phonebook Access Profile exposes the contact database to any bonded device. On an unattended device this is a data-disclosure path.
checks.remediation: Disable the profile in the product build: set persist.bluetooth.profile.pbap.server.enabled=false, or remove it from the enabled profile list in the Bluetooth APEX config, then reboot.

checks.label: bluetooth.sap Property
checks.command: S=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); V=$(getprop persist.bluetooth.profile.sap.server.enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] && V=$(getprop bluetooth.profile.sap.server.enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] && V=$(getprop bluetooth.sap 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$V" ] && [ -z "$S" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED getprop unavailable"; elif [ -z "$V" ]; then echo "sap=not_set"; else echo "sap=$V"; fi
checks.description: SIM Access Profile lets a paired device read the SIM directly, including IMSI and the ability to place calls on the subscriber identity. It has no purpose on a kiosk, panel or POS terminal and should be off.
checks.remediation: Disable the profile in the product build: set persist.bluetooth.profile.sap.server.enabled=false, or remove it from the enabled profile list in the Bluetooth APEX config, then reboot.

checks.label: bluetooth.map Property
checks.command: S=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); V=$(getprop persist.bluetooth.profile.map.server.enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] && V=$(getprop bluetooth.profile.map.server.enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] && V=$(getprop bluetooth.map 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$V" ] && [ -z "$S" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED getprop unavailable"; elif [ -z "$V" ]; then echo "map=not_set"; else echo "map=$V"; fi
checks.description: Message Access Profile exposes SMS and messaging content to bonded devices. No check covered this namespace before.
checks.remediation: Set persist.bluetooth.profile.map.server.enabled=false and reboot.

checks.label: bluetooth.secure Property
checks.description: Bluetooth secure mode should be enabled (property).
checks.remediation: Enable Bluetooth secure mode: setprop bluetooth.secure true.

checks.label: Bluetooth Version ≥ 5.0
checks.description: Bluetooth version should be 5.0 or newer to support LE Secure Connections and mitigate SweynTooth/BLESA.
checks.remediation: Upgrade device firmware to support Bluetooth 5.0+ for LE Secure Connections.

checks.label: Bluetooth Debug Properties
checks.description: No debug-related Bluetooth properties should be set; they disable security checks and expose test interfaces.
checks.remediation: Remove all debug BT properties: setprop <debug_property> "" for each found property (requires root).

checks.label: Bluetooth Stack Crash Log
checks.description: No recent Bluetooth crashes in the log; crashes may indicate exploitation attempts like BlueFrag (CVE-2020-0022).
checks.remediation: Investigate crash logs for exploitation indicators. Apply latest security patches to address known BT CVEs.

checks.label: Raw HCI Device Nodes Unexposed
checks.description: Counts raw Bluetooth HCI transport nodes. The earlier version also globbed /dev/radio*, which on a Samsung device matches /dev/radio0, the FM radio node, and has nothing to do with Bluetooth HCI. That produced a finding on any device with an FM tuner.
checks.remediation: Remove exposed HCI device nodes: rm /dev/hci* /dev/radio* (requires root). Verify kernel config.

checks.label: Bluetooth Firmware Present
checks.command: if ! ls /vendor >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! ls /system >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "UNMEASURED /vendor and /system both unlistable"; else ls /vendor/bt_firmware/image/* /vendor/firmware/*bt* /vendor/firmware/crbtfw* /vendor/etc/firmware/*bt* /system/etc/firmware/*bt* /firmware/image/*bt* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; fi
checks.description: At least one Bluetooth firmware file should exist. Searches the dedicated /vendor/bt_firmware partition used by Qualcomm as well as the generic firmware directories; absence across all of them may indicate tampering or custom radio firmware.
checks.remediation: Verify firmware files are intact. Restore from factory image if missing or tampered.

checks.label: Custom Vendor BT Libraries
checks.command: if ! ls /vendor >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! ls /system >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "UNMEASURED /vendor and /system both unlistable"; else ls /vendor/lib*/hw/*bluetooth* /system/lib*/hw/*bluetooth* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; fi
checks.description: At least one vendor Bluetooth HAL library should exist; absence or unexpected files may indicate tampering or supply chain risk.
checks.remediation: Verify vendor BT HAL libraries are intact. Restore from factory image if missing or unexpected.

checks.label: Apps with BLUETOOTH Permission
checks.command: D=$(pm list permissions -g -d 2>/dev/null); case "$D" in ""|*"Can't find service"*|*"Failure calling service"*|*"Failed transaction"*|*"does not exist"*|*"Found 0 services"*) echo "UNMEASURED pm list permissions -g -d did not answer";; *) printf '%s\n' "$D" | grep -A1 'BLUETOOTH$' | grep -c 'package:';; esac
checks.description: Too many apps (10+) with BLUETOOTH permission increases risk. Zero is safe.
checks.remediation: Revoke BLUETOOTH permission from unnecessary apps: pm revoke <package> android.permission.BLUETOOTH.

checks.label: Apps with BLUETOOTH_ADMIN Permission
checks.command: D=$(pm list permissions -g -d 2>/dev/null); case "$D" in ""|*"Can't find service"*|*"Failure calling service"*|*"Failed transaction"*|*"does not exist"*|*"Found 0 services"*) echo "UNMEASURED pm list permissions -g -d did not answer";; *) printf '%s\n' "$D" | grep -A1 'BLUETOOTH_ADMIN$' | grep -c 'package:';; esac
checks.description: Fewer than three apps should hold BLUETOOTH_ADMIN; excess apps can toggle Bluetooth, clear bonds, and change scan mode.
checks.remediation: Revoke BLUETOOTH_ADMIN from unnecessary apps: pm revoke <package> android.permission.BLUETOOTH_ADMIN.

checks.label: Auto‑enable Bluetooth
checks.description: Bluetooth should not automatically turn on (NIST AC‑18)
checks.remediation: Disable Bluetooth auto-enable: settings put global bluetooth_auto_on 0.

checks.label: BR/EDR Secure Connections Enforcement
checks.command: V=$(settings get global bluetooth_br_edr_secure_connections 2>/dev/null); case "$V" in 1) echo Enforced;; 0) echo NotEnforced;; *) echo UNMEASURED;; esac
checks.description: BR/EDR Secure Connections must be enforced to prevent the KNOB attack (CVE-2019-9506).
checks.remediation: Enforce BR/EDR Secure Connections: settings put global bluetooth_br_edr_secure_connections 1.

checks.label: Discoverable Mode
checks.description: Device should not be discoverable (AC-18)
checks.remediation: Disable discoverable mode: settings put global bluetooth_discoverability 0.

checks.label: BT Device Name Info Leakage
checks.description: Bluetooth device name should be null or generic; names revealing model, owner, or organization aid OSINT and targeted attacks.
checks.remediation: Set a generic BT name: settings put secure bluetooth_name "Device". Avoid personal or org-identifying names.

checks.label: Bluetooth HID Host Role (accepts input devices)
checks.command: S=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); V=$(getprop persist.bluetooth.profile.hid.host.enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] && V=$(getprop bluetooth.profile.hid.host.enabled 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$V" ] && [ -z "$S" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED getprop unavailable"; elif [ -z "$V" ]; then echo "hid_host=not_set"; else echo "hid_host=$V"; fi
checks.description: The device accepts Bluetooth keyboards and mice. On an unattended kiosk, panel, POS terminal or digital-signage unit this is a physical-proximity input path: an attacker in radio range pairs an input device and types directly into the UI. It is also the precondition for the unauthenticated HID keystroke-injection class (CVE-2023-45866), where a host that accepts HID connections can be driven without completing user-confirmed pairing. Expected true on a general-purpose phone or tablet, expected false on a fixed install with no keyboard.
checks.remediation: Set persist.bluetooth.profile.hid.host.enabled=false in the product build and reboot. If a keyboard is genuinely required, confirm the security patch level covers CVE-2023-45866 and restrict pairing to a provisioning mode rather than leaving the host role always on.

checks.label: Bluetooth HID Device Role (acts as an input device)
checks.command: S=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); V=$(getprop persist.bluetooth.profile.hid.device.enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] && V=$(getprop bluetooth.profile.hid.device.enabled 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$V" ] && [ -z "$S" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED getprop unavailable"; elif [ -z "$V" ]; then echo "hid_device=not_set"; else echo "hid_device=$V"; fi
checks.description: The device can present itself as a Bluetooth keyboard or mouse to another host. Any code running here can then inject keystrokes into whatever it is paired with, crossing from this device into a workstation or another terminal. Almost never intentional outside of purpose-built peripherals.
checks.remediation: Set persist.bluetooth.profile.hid.device.enabled=false in the product build and reboot.

checks.label: Bluetooth Radio rfkill State
checks.command: B=""; for d in /sys/class/rfkill/rfkill*; do [ "$(cat $d/type 2>/dev/null)" = bluetooth ] && B=$d && break; done; if [ -z "$B" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no rfkill node of type bluetooth"; else S=$(cat "$B/soft" 2>/dev/null); H=$(cat "$B/hard" 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$S$H" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED rfkill node present but unreadable"; else echo "bt_soft_block=${S:-?} bt_hard_block=${H:-?}"; fi; fi
checks.description: rfkill reports whether the Bluetooth radio is currently blocked, read straight from sysfs with no framework involvement. soft_block=1 means the radio is disabled in software. On a fixed-function device with no Bluetooth requirement the radio should be blocked; an unblocked radio is live attack surface reachable from physical proximity. Compare this against the framework's bluetooth_on setting: the two disagreeing means something re-enabled the radio outside the normal settings path.
checks.remediation: If Bluetooth is not required, block the radio at boot (rfkill block bluetooth, or disable the BT HAL service in the product init rc) rather than relying on the framework toggle alone.

checks.label: Bluetooth Controller Identification
checks.command: B=""; for d in /sys/class/rfkill/rfkill*; do [ "$(cat $d/type 2>/dev/null)" = bluetooth ] && B=$d && break; done; if [ -z "$B" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no rfkill node of type bluetooth"; else N=$(cat "$B/name" 2>/dev/null); P=$(readlink -f "$B" 2>/dev/null); D=$(basename $(dirname $(dirname "$P")) 2>/dev/null); echo "rfkill_name=${N:-unknown} controller=${D:-unknown}"; fi
checks.description: Identifies the Bluetooth controller from the rfkill device path in sysfs. The controller model is what determines which firmware-level Bluetooth CVEs apply, and it is readable without the framework, so this still answers on a transport where dumpsys is unreachable.
checks.remediation: Informational. Use the controller identifier to check vendor advisories for that specific Bluetooth chipset.

checks.label: L2CAP ERTM Disabled (BlueBorne CVE-2017-1000251 mitigation)
checks.command: V=$(cat /sys/module/bluetooth/parameters/disable_ertm 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$V" ]; then echo "disable_ertm=$V"; elif ls /sys/module/bluetooth >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "ERTM_PARAM_ABSENT"; else echo "UNMEASURED bluetooth kernel module not present in sysfs"; fi
checks.description: The kernel L2CAP Enhanced Retransmission Mode is the code path exploited by CVE-2017-1000251 (BlueBorne, stack buffer overflow in the Linux L2CAP config parser). Setting the bluetooth module parameter disable_ertm=Y removes that path entirely and is the standard mitigation on devices that do not need ERTM. disable_ertm=N means the code path is reachable; whether it is exploitable depends on the kernel version, so treat this as attack-surface reduction rather than proof of vulnerability.
checks.remediation: Set the module parameter at boot: add bluetooth.disable_ertm=Y to the kernel command line, or write Y to /sys/module/bluetooth/parameters/disable_ertm. Confirm no paired peripheral requires ERTM first.

checks.label: eSCO Link Disabled
checks.command: V=$(cat /sys/module/bluetooth/parameters/disable_esco 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$V" ]; then echo "disable_esco=$V"; elif ls /sys/module/bluetooth >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "ESCO_PARAM_ABSENT"; else echo "UNMEASURED bluetooth kernel module not present in sysfs"; fi
checks.description: Reports whether extended SCO links are disabled at the kernel module level. eSCO carries synchronous audio; it is only needed on devices doing hands-free or headset audio and is additional link-layer surface elsewhere.
checks.remediation: Informational unless the device has no audio role, in which case set bluetooth.disable_esco=Y on the kernel command line.

checks.label: Bluetooth Controller Firmware Version
checks.command: F=$(cat /vendor/bt_firmware/image/*.ver /vendor/firmware/*bt*.ver 2>/dev/null | head -1); N=$(ls /vendor/bt_firmware/image/ /vendor/firmware/*bt* 2>/dev/null | wc -l); if [ -n "$F" ]; then echo "bt_fw=$F files=$N"; elif ls /vendor >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "BT_FW_VERSION_NOT_PRESENT files=$N"; else echo "UNMEASURED /vendor not listable"; fi
checks.description: Reads the Bluetooth controller firmware build string from the vendor firmware image directory. Controller firmware is patched separately from the Android security patch level, so a current SPL does not imply current Bluetooth firmware. Readable without the framework.
checks.remediation: Informational. Compare the firmware build against the chipset vendor's current release and confirm it postdates the controller advisories that apply.

checks.label: Bluetooth Stack Trace Verbosity
checks.command: C=$(cat /apex/com.android.btservices/etc/bluetooth/bt_stack.conf /system/etc/bluetooth/bt_stack.conf /vendor/etc/bluetooth/bt_stack.conf 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$C" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no readable bt_stack.conf"; else T=$(printf '%s\n' "$C" | grep -c '^TRC_[A-Z_]*=[456]'); E=$(printf '%s\n' "$C" | grep -i '^TraceConf' | head -1); echo "verbose_trace_modules=$T ${E:-TraceConf=unset}"; fi
checks.description: bt_stack.conf sets the per-module trace level for the Bluetooth stack. Levels 4 to 6 (DEBUG through VERBOSE) cause the stack to log link keys, addresses and protocol payloads to the system log, which any process able to read logs can then harvest. Level 2 (WARNING) is the shipping default. Read directly from the config file, so this answers without the framework.
checks.remediation: Set every TRC_* entry in bt_stack.conf to 2 or lower and rebuild the Bluetooth APEX or vendor image. Do not ship a build with stack tracing raised.

checks.label: Bluetooth Bonded Device Store Not World-Readable
checks.command: P=""; for d in /data/misc/bluedroid /data/vendor/bluetooth /data/misc/bluetooth; do ls -d "$d" >/dev/null 2>&1 && P="$P $d"; done; if [ -z "$P" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED bonded-device directories not listable from this context"; else R=""; for d in $P; do ls "$d" >/dev/null 2>&1 && R="$R $d"; done; [ -n "$R" ] && echo "READABLE_BOND_STORE:$R" || echo "BOND_STORE_PROTECTED:$P"; fi
checks.description: bt_config.conf under the Bluetooth data directory holds the adapter address, every bonded peer and their link keys. A shell that can read it can clone the pairing relationship and decrypt or impersonate links. On a correctly labelled device the directory is confined to the bluetooth domain and even a root shell in another domain is refused. A denied read is reported as UNMEASURED rather than as a pass, because SELinux denies stat as well as read and an absent directory and a protected one look identical to a naive test.
checks.remediation: Confirm the bonded-device directory carries the bluetooth_data_file label and that no non-bluetooth domain has read access in the shipping policy.

checks.label: Bluetooth HAL Interface Version
checks.command: H=$(ls /vendor/bin/hw/ 2>/dev/null | grep -i 'hardware.bluetooth' | head -3 | tr '\n' ' '); if [ -z "$H" ]; then if ls /vendor/bin/hw >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "NO_BLUETOOTH_HAL_BINARY"; else echo "UNMEASURED /vendor/bin/hw not listable"; fi; else echo "bt_hal=$H"; fi
checks.description: Reports which Bluetooth HAL implementation is installed. HIDL @1.0 is the original interface; @1.1 added controller error reporting and current builds use the AIDL interface. An old HIDL revision on a recent platform usually means the vendor Bluetooth stack has not been refreshed alongside the framework.
checks.remediation: Informational. Where the platform supports it, move the vendor implementation to the AIDL Bluetooth HAL so it receives current fixes.

checks.label: Bluetooth Stack Process Not Running As Root
checks.command: P=$( (ps -A -o user,name 2>/dev/null || /system/bin/ps -A -o user,name 2>/dev/null) ); if [ -z "$P" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no process listing available"; else B=$(printf '%s\n' "$P" | grep -iE 'com[.]android[.]bluetooth|hardware[.]bluetooth'); if [ -z "$B" ]; then echo "BLUETOOTH_STACK_NOT_RUNNING"; elif printf '%s\n' "$B" | grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*root[[:space:]]'; then echo "ROOT_BLUETOOTH_PROCESS"; else echo "BT_PROCESS_UNPRIVILEGED"; fi; fi
checks.description: The Bluetooth stack and its HAL parse attacker-reachable radio input, so they must not run as root. AOSP runs both as the dedicated bluetooth uid. A root Bluetooth process turns any parsing bug in the stack into full system compromise. Read from the process list, so it answers without the framework.
checks.remediation: Run the Bluetooth app and HAL service as the bluetooth uid in the product init rc, never as root.

checks.label: Bluetooth Profile Toggle Helper Not Shell-Executable
checks.command: S=$(ls -l /vendor/bin/bluetooth_sink_role /vendor/bin/*bt_role* /vendor/bin/*bluetooth*role* 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$S" ]; then if ls /vendor/bin >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "NO_PROFILE_TOGGLE_HELPER"; else echo "UNMEASURED /vendor/bin not listable"; fi; else printf '%s\n' "$S" | grep -E '^-...(.)?.?x' && echo "SHELL_EXECUTABLE_TOGGLE_HELPER" || echo "TOGGLE_HELPER_RESTRICTED"; fi
checks.description: Some vendor images ship a helper script that flips Bluetooth profiles by writing persist.bluetooth.profile.* properties and broadcasting an unbond intent. When that script is group or world executable, any shell on the device can change which Bluetooth profiles the platform exposes and can force-clear existing bonds, without going through settings or any permission check.
checks.remediation: Restrict the helper to root only (0700, root:root) or remove it from production images and perform profile selection at build time.

checks.label: Kernel Bluetooth HCI Device Exposure
checks.command: if ! ls -d /sys/class/bluetooth >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "UNMEASURED /sys/class/bluetooth not listable"; else N=$(ls /sys/class/bluetooth/ 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'hci'); echo "kernel_hci_devices=$N"; fi
checks.description: Android drives Bluetooth through a userspace HAL, so no kernel HCI device should be registered under /sys/class/bluetooth. An hci interface present here means a BlueZ-style kernel path is active alongside or instead of the Android stack, which exposes the kernel L2CAP, RFCOMM and SCO implementations directly and is usually a sign of a debug or vendor-bringup configuration left enabled.
checks.remediation: Identify what registered the HCI device (a btusb, btsdio or hci_uart driver) and remove it from the shipping kernel configuration if the platform uses the Android userspace stack.
